names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 29 Οκτωβρίου, «Οσία Άννα η μετονομασθείσα Eυφημιανός», with the rank word left off. The page glosses the name from the Hebrew Hannah, favour and grace.
The name she took in the men's monastery, printed in the same line of saint.gr's calendar for 29 Οκτωβρίου: «η μετονομασθείσα Eυφημιανός», and in the notice «με το ψευδώνυμο: Ευφημιανός».

Read out of the heading on the first of her two life pages, «Преподобная Анна Вифинская», with the rank word left off; her name link carries the same title. The day line gives the forename alone with the monastic name in brackets, «Прп. Анны (Евфимиана)», and no province.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru prints «(826)» after her name on 29 октября ст. ст., and both of its lives give the year in words: «скончалась в Константинополе в 826 г.» and «Скончалась преподобная Анна в Константинополе в 826 году». The Greek page this folder was written from gave no year.

feast.note: The first of her two life pages is headed «Дни памяти: 13 июня , 29 октября». One row per church is the schema, so the June day is recorded here and she does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 октября ст. ст. — «Прп. Анны (Евфимиана) (826).»
source.note: The line is the fourth of the day and carries no typikon icon, so no rank is recorded.

attestations.note: The Russian is the first calendar to give this folder a date, and it gives the whole of her story: a deacon of the Blachernae church at Constantinople for a father, a husband dead, the man's monastic habit put on and the name Euphemianos taken, a Bithynian house near Olympus for a home, the gift of wonders in her own lifetime, and a death at Constantinople in 826. **Her son is named in both lives and in the second one's title, «Преподобная Анна и сын ее святой Иоанн», and the calendar's own line names only her**, so no folder is made for him and this is written down instead.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Οκτωβρίου — «Οσία Άννα η μετονομασθείσα Eυφημιανός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The corpus keeps ten other Annas and none of them is this one: the daughter of a deacon John of the Blachernae, widowed, who entered a men's monastery under the name Euphemianos in the time of Leo the Isaurian. No location is recorded although the page names Byzantium and the Blachernae, because it names no place of her monastery. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (1 October 2026).
